open_questions.text: The EMAIL_HASH_PEPPER_ACTIVE value in the running environment is byte-identical to the placeholder committed in .env.example (v1:change-me-in-every-real-environment). The keyed HMAC protecting identity_account.email_hash is therefore unkeyed against anyone holding the repo, and the single-campus email space is small enough to enumerate exhaustively. Combined with SEC-002 (no TLS to the Supabase host) and SEC-003 (no RLS on any table) on an instance already holding real user data, this is a live deanonymization path for every registered student. A human must decide and execute the pepper rotation (runbooks/pepper-rotation.md has 6 unfilled [HUMAN: markers, task T72) and must decide whether existing real rows require re-hashing or purging under the DPDP posture (RR-10). Not designed around, not waived by this agent.

Neither gitleaks nor osv-scanner is installed on this host, and semgrep --config auto cannot reach its registry (TLS egress interception: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED to semgrep.dev, CRYPT_E_NO_REVOCATION_CHECK to github.com releases). Substitutes ran (detect-secrets 1.5.0, npm audit, a 10-rule self-authored semgrep ruleset) and are reported, but the mandated Layer-1 toolchain has never produced a signal on this repo, because the ci.yml workflow that would run it has never executed: there is no git remote. A human must add a remote or provision the three tools locally before T62, which cadence.md makes blocking, runs on the same degraded evidence.

tests/nfr/identity-nondisclosure.test.ts (T55) could not be executed: it hard-fails without DATABASE_URL by design, and the only reachable database holds real user data that its beforeEach would TRUNCATE. The T55 green claim rests on a run with no artifact in the repo. A disposable test database is a prerequisite for T62 and every later NFR gate.

Whether Supabase's PostgREST API is enabled on the project behind DATABASE_URL could not be verified from the codebase; it determines whether SEC-003 is a defence-in-depth gap or a directly exploitable anonymous read of identity_account. Requires Supabase dashboard access.

SEC-008 (A1 account-existence oracle) is a product decision as much as a security one: suppressing the 409 costs the S4 'already registered' copy that docs/04-ux.md F1 specifies. Whether membership disclosure is acceptable for a product whose premise is anonymity is a human call.

docs/08-security.md could not be written: the repo guardrail freezes docs/08-* because later-stage docs (docs/14-resilience.md, docs/16-privacy.md) already exist, and unlocking requires a human to add '08' to .pipeline/unlock. This agent did not bypass the guardrail. The full stage-08 handoff is parked at .pipeline/sec/handoff-08-security.json and the gate record at docs/gates/security-gate-M1.json; a human must unlock 08 (or re-order the pipeline) for the stage doc to be authored.

tool_runs.report_path: (none - SSLError CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED reaching semgrep.dev/c/auto; default registry ruleset never ran)

tool_runs.invocation: semgrep scan --config .pipeline/sec/local-rules.yaml --json --output .pipeline/sec/semgrep-local.json --metrics=off --exclude node_modules server client tests scripts

tool_runs.report_path: (none - command not found; binary download blocked by TLS interception, CRYPT_E_NO_REVOCATION_CHECK)

tool_runs.invocation: git rev-list --all | while read c; do git grep -nIE '(AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}|ghp_[A-Za-z0-9]{36}|sk-[A-Za-z0-9]{32,}|-----BEGIN [A-Z ]*PRIVATE KEY-----|xox[baprs]-[0-9A-Za-z-]{10,}|AIza[0-9A-Za-z_-]{35}|SG\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,})' $c; done  # 0 hits over 14 commits; plus git log --diff-filter=A -- .env (empty)

tool_runs.report_path: (none - command not found; trivy fallback also not installed)

tool_runs.invocation: npx vitest run tests/unit  # 35/35 pass; DB-touching suites deliberately not run (live DB holds real data)

findings.evidence: sha256 of the live .env value equals sha256 of the value committed in tracked .env.example (v1:change-me-in-every-real-environment); comparison done by digest, values never printed. email_hash = HMAC-SHA256(pepper, normalized_email) over a single allowlisted campus domain with structured roll-number local parts - a candidate space in the thousands. With the pepper public, any exposure of identity_account.email_hash or ban_record.email_hash deanonymizes every user by exhaustive enumeration. Three exposure paths exist in this same codebase today: SEC-002, SEC-003, and a database already holding real user data. Nullifies the T50/RR-7/RR-13 control set.
findings.provenance: manual:crypto-key-triage (env-vs-example digest comparison) + code read email-identity.ts:103
findings.fix_hint: Generate a fresh high-entropy v2: pepper per environment from a secrets manager; move v1: to EMAIL_HASH_PEPPER_RETIRED and run the dual-hash rollout in runbooks/pepper-rotation.md (6 unfilled [HUMAN: markers, T72). Remove the secret-shaped placeholder from .env.example and add a config startup assertion refusing known-placeholder values. Pin with SECREG-SEC-001.

findings.location: server/src/db/pool.ts:8-13; .env DATABASE_URL host db.yinckproedjodpbvzdhb.supabase.co:5432, sslmode unset
findings.evidence: new pg.Pool({connectionString, max, idleTimeoutMillis, connectionTimeoutMillis}) passes no ssl option and the connection string carries no sslmode parameter; node-postgres defaults to no TLS in this configuration. The host is a remote Supabase instance reached over the public internet, so the DB password, every email_hash, every email_encrypted blob and every OTP hash traverse the network in cleartext.
findings.provenance: manual:transport-security - code read pool.ts:8-13 + DATABASE_URL parse (host/port/sslmode only, credentials not read)
findings.fix_hint: Set ssl: { rejectUnauthorized: true, ca: <supabase root CA> } in pool.ts and ?sslmode=verify-full in every environment's DATABASE_URL; enable Enforce SSL on the Supabase project. Pin with SECREG-SEC-002.

findings.category: A01:2021 Broken Access Control - default-open storage rules
findings.evidence: grep -niE 'row level security|create policy|grant |revoke |security definer' server/migrations/ returns 0 matches across all migrations. identity_account (email_hash, email_encrypted, verification_token_hash) is created in the default public schema of a Supabase-hosted database with no RLS and no policies; on Supabase, public-schema tables are exposed via PostgREST to anon/service_role key holders and RLS is the only barrier. The 'never joined into any user-facing read path' comment at 001_identity.up.sql:20 is an application-layer statement PostgREST does not honour.
findings.provenance: manual:storage-rules (security-audit skill Method step 3, Supabase RLS class) - grep over server/migrations/
findings.fix_hint: ENABLE + FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY on all 14 tables as they land; REVOKE ALL from anon/authenticated. The app connects as owner and is unaffected. Pin with SECREG-SEC-003 (assert pg_class.relrowsecurity for every public table after migrate up).

findings.category: A07:2021 Authentication Failures - missing brute-force protection
findings.evidence: confirmVerification never reads or writes verification_attempt_count, and identity.repo.ts exposes no increment-on-failure function - the counter is set only on the send path (createPending sets 1, reissueToken sets the caller's value). No rate-limit middleware exists anywhere (no express-rate-limit in package.json). OTP is crypto.randomInt(0,1e6), a 10^6 space with a 15-minute TTL. Attack: submit a victim's campus email to A1 (which requires no proof of address control), then brute-force A2; at ~500 req/s the keyspace is exhausted inside the TTL. The attacker completes registration as the victim's email, obtains a verified year badge and a session, and the victim is permanently locked out with 409 email_already_registered.
findings.provenance: manual:authn-bruteforce - control-flow read of identity.service.ts:126-174 + grep verification_attempt_count over identity.repo.ts + package.json dependency inventory
findings.fix_hint: Increment verification_attempt_count on every failed A2 confirm in the same transaction; invalidate the token past ~5 failures; add per-IP express-rate-limit on /verification/* as an independent second layer. Pin with SECREG-SEC-004.

findings.category: A09:2021 Security Logging Failures - credential written to logs
findings.evidence: Empirically verified against this repo's installed pino-http: a harness using the same pinoHttp call shape, sent Authorization: Bearer SECRET-SESSION-TOKEN-ABC123, emitted the token verbatim (LEAK CONFIRMED). logger.ts redacts email/email_hash/token/verification_token_hash and one-level wildcards but NOT req.headers.authorization, and pino-http's default req serializer emits the whole headers object (visible in this run's unit-test output). The session token is a 30-day sliding credential (config.sessionTtlDays=30, session.ts:38), so anyone with log read access impersonates that pseudonymous user for a month with sliding refresh extending it. POST /session/exchange logs the bootstrap token identically.
findings.provenance: manual:log-leakage - empirical reproduction against pino-http as installed, plus code read logger.ts:11-25 and app.ts:19
findings.fix_hint: Add req.headers.authorization, req.headers.cookie and res.headers['x-session-refresh'] to redact.paths, or pass serializers.req whitelisting method/url/id. One-line fix; highest severity-to-effort ratio in this report. Pin with SECREG-SEC-005.

findings.category: A09:2021 / insecure default - plaintext OTP to stdout
findings.evidence: config falls back to EMAIL_PROVIDER='console'; ConsoleEmailProvider.sendVerification console.logs the raw recipient address and the raw OTP on one line (its own comment says 'Never do this in prod' but nothing enforces it). baseProvider() routes unknown values to UnconfiguredProvider (throws, fail-loud) but routes the ABSENT value to console (fail-silent) - A1 then returns 202 as though mail was sent. The 'memory' provider's claim that it is 'guarded by the env switch below' is false: no guard exists. The live .env is EMAIL_PROVIDER=console with NODE_ENV=development against a database holding real user data - this is the configuration the T11 tracer demo will run.
findings.provenance: semgrep@1.172.0:local-secret-in-log-or-response at server/src/modules/notification/email-provider.ts:27, plus manual:env-triage (digest match to .env.example, resolved value 'console')
findings.fix_hint: Make EMAIL_PROVIDER a required() var with no fallback; have baseProvider() throw when console/memory is selected outside NODE_ENV development/test. Pin with SECREG-SEC-006.

findings.category: A04:2021 Insecure Design - missing rate limiting on signup/OTP path
findings.location: server/src/modules/identity/identity.service.ts:32-96 - the cooldown/window block at :60-78 sits inside if (existing); the createPending path at :86-95 has none
findings.evidence: The resend cooldown and verificationMaxAttemptsPerWindow=5 budget are keyed on an existing identity_account row, so a request for an address with no row skips all of it: hash, createPending, send a real email. Each distinct address is a fresh budget and no middleware backstops it (no rate-limit package in package.json). An unauthenticated attacker iterating roll-number-shaped addresses at the single allowlisted domain produces one real outbound email per request: mass unsolicited mail from Murmur's sending domain to real students, uncapped SMTP spend, uncapped identity_account row creation, and pre-registration of every predictable campus address (locking those students out per SEC-004). The T7 trace promises 'rate limiting + attempt counters' on A1 unconditionally.
findings.provenance: manual:rate-limit-coverage - control-flow read of initiateVerification + package.json dependency inventory
findings.fix_hint: Per-IP express-rate-limit on /verification/initiate before the service call, plus a global per-window ceiling on new-account creation; the per-account window then remains the second layer it was designed to be. Pin with SECREG-SEC-007.

findings.evidence: A1 returns three behaviourally distinct outcomes - 202 (new), 409 (registered), 429 (pending within cooldown) - so an unauthenticated caller learns whether any given campus address has a Murmur account. For a product whose premise is that nobody knows you use it, membership disclosure is the exact question a hostile peer or administrator would ask, and SEC-007 leaves nothing to slow whole-campus enumeration. tests/nfr/identity-nondisclosure.test.ts:88-142 covers five branches and never exercises the duplicate branch, so this is not a regression T55 would catch.
findings.provenance: manual:enumeration - code read identity.service.ts:51-58 + coverage read of tests/nfr/identity-nondisclosure.test.ts
findings.fix_hint: Return an identical 202 verification_pending shape for new, pending and already-registered addresses; deliver an 'you already have an account' email instead of signalling in the HTTP response, or gate the S4 refused copy behind the confirmed-OTP step. Pin with SECREG-SEC-008.

findings.category: A01:2021 Broken Access Control - unauthenticated write with spoofable actor
findings.evidence: eventSchema accepts actorProfileId (uuid, optional) and metadata (arbitrary record) from any anonymous caller and writes both to analytics_event. The six PRD metrics gating R8 are computed from this table by T46, so an outsider can forge Murmur's launch metrics and the M6 traceability audit would find the derivation sound. Secondary: unbounded row growth capped only by the 256kb body limit. The public half of the route is a deliberate product decision (pre-registration funnel events on S1); the defect is trusting a client-supplied actorProfileId.
findings.provenance: manual:authz-surface - route/middleware inventory across app.ts:31-38 and analytics.routes.ts:13-34
findings.fix_hint: Run the route through an optional-session middleware, ignore any client-supplied actorProfileId and stamp it server-side from req.profile (null when anonymous); add per-IP rate limiting and an eventType allowlist. Pin with SECREG-SEC-009.

findings.category: A05:2021 Security Misconfiguration - missing security headers
findings.evidence: No helmet in package.json dependencies and no app.disable('x-powered-by'). Observed in this run's unit-test log output: every response carries x-powered-by: Express. No HSTS, no X-Content-Type-Options, no frame-ancestors, no Referrer-Policy, no CSP. The missing CSP is the material one given the session credential lives in localStorage (SEC-013).
findings.provenance: manual:headers - dependency inventory + response headers captured in npx vitest run tests/unit output
findings.fix_hint: app.use(helmet()) and app.disable('x-powered-by'). Pin with SECREG-SEC-010 (assert HSTS, nosniff and CSP present and x-powered-by absent on GET /health).

findings.evidence: key() returns null when unconfigured and encryptEmail() then returns null, so identity_account.email_encrypted is written NULL. This fails safe for confidentiality but fails silently, breaking two documented behaviours: the transient raw-email retention described at 001_identity.up.sql:24 and the module docstring, and the manual-fallback review of blocked_unparseable_year registrations that T41 will consume (the operator will have no address to contact). Nothing at startup or in /health reports the control is off. Confirmed by key-presence inventory of .env (names and set/empty only; values not read).
findings.fix_hint: Require the key when NODE_ENV !== development; surface email_encryption: 'disabled' in /health so the state is observable. Pin with SECREG-SEC-011.

findings.evidence: npm audit full tree: critical 1, high 10, moderate 3. npm audit --omit=dev: 0 of every severity - the production dependency tree is clean. Triage with evidence: every advisory resolves to a devDependencies path (vitest -> @vitest/mocker/vite/vite-node; eslint -> @eslint/eslintrc/minimatch/brace-expansion; glob/rimraf/flat-cache). The critical is GHSA-5xrq-8626-4rwp (Vitest UI arbitrary file read/execute) and requires the Vitest UI server, which this project never starts (scripts use 'vitest run' only). Held at medium rather than dropped because GHSA-4w7w-66w2-5vf9 and GHSA-fx2h-pf6j-xcff are Vite dev-server path-traversal issues specific to Windows, which is this developer's platform, and vite dev is run routinely.
findings.provenance: npm@10.9.2:audit (.pipeline/sec/npm-audit.json) and npm@10.9.2:audit --omit=dev (.pipeline/sec/npm-audit-prod.json); recorded as osv-scanner fallback per security-audit skill Method step 1
findings.fix_hint: npm audit fix (minor vitest/vite bumps; eslint 8->9 is the only non-trivial one) before the M6 gate so T48's re-scan is clean. SCA is a CI gate, not a unit test - restore the sca job (SEC-014) rather than writing a SECREG- test.

findings.category: A05:2021 / A03 XSS blast radius - unenforced premise behind the session-storage decision
findings.evidence: The OQ-14 decision accepts localStorage partly because 'the XSS control is the client's own attack surface: no third-party scripts, and the design components are static markup.' Two things weaken that premise: there is no CSP at all (SEC-010), so the premise is a convention rather than a control; and client/src/components/support.js - vendored Claude Design runtime, in-tree - fetches unpkg.com React/Babel and executes fetched source via new Function(...) at :774 and :1148. Triaged down from high: it is reachable only from 'Landing Page.dc.html', while client/index.html loads /src/main.ts only, which never imports components/ (verified by grep). It is not in the built app, but it is served by the Vite dev server. Blast radius given SEC-005 and a 30-day sliding token: one XSS equals a month of impersonation, silently renewed.
findings.provenance: semgrep@1.172.0:local-dangerous-dynamic-eval (support.js:774, :1148) + manual:client-surface (entry-graph read of index.html and main.ts)
findings.fix_hint: Ship a CSP (script-src 'self'; style-src 'self' fonts.googleapis.com) alongside SEC-010's headers; keep .dc.html preview harnesses out of the served root. Pin with SECREG-SEC-013 (assert the built dist/ entry graph contains no new Function/eval and no unpkg.com reference).

findings.category: Process - designated blocking control has never executed
findings.location: .github/workflows/ci.yml jobs secrets-scan, sast, sca; git remote -v is empty
findings.evidence: cadence.md section 1 designates gitleaks 'BLOCKING from first run. No warn-only period - a committed secret is never a warning.' That gate has produced zero signal: the workflow has never run because there is no git remote (14 local commits, no .git/refs/remotes). The same holds for the sast and sca jobs. Plan task T3 is marked complete and traces Layer-1 coverage from day one; in reality Layer 1 was unexecuted for all of M1, which is why SEC-001 survived to be found at the milestone gate rather than on the commit that introduced it. Two further defects for when it does run: sast and sca both carry continue-on-error: true, contradicting cadence.md section 1's blocking designation for SCA; and the sca step scans only the root package-lock.json, never client/package-lock.json.
findings.provenance: manual:ci-verification - git remote -v (empty) + read of .github/workflows/ci.yml against cadence.md section 1
findings.fix_hint: Add a remote and push, or run the three scanners in a local pre-push hook. Remove continue-on-error from sca, reconcile the sast comment with section 1, and add the client lockfile to the osv-scanner invocation.

findings.category: A07:2021 - token replay; documentation asserts a property the code lacks
findings.evidence: issue() builds {sub, typ, iat, exp} with no jti and /session/exchange performs no consumption bookkeeping, so the same bootstrap token mints unlimited session tokens until exp. session.ts:13 documents it as 'exchangeable once' and client/src/api.ts:108-111 repeats the claim. Impact is genuinely low - the token is handed only to the user who just proved address control, TTL is 15 minutes, and the exchange re-reads live profile status (session.routes.ts:36-39), which is a good control - but SEC-005 puts that token in the logs.
findings.provenance: manual:token-lifecycle - code read session.ts:77-87 and session.routes.ts:27-45 against the docstrings
findings.fix_hint: Prefer amending the three docstrings to 'usable until expiry' over building a jti/nonce store for a 15-minute credential.

findings.evidence: console.log('No identity_account found for ' + email) and the deletion confirmation print the operator-supplied raw address; the address is also on the process command line (shell history, process table). Operator-run rather than request-path, but it is raw identity material outside the hash/encryption boundary - exactly what the T61 privacy leakage baseline sweeps for.
findings.fix_hint: Log h.hash (already computed at :17) instead of email; read the address from stdin rather than argv.

findings.category: Operational safety - destructive test guard is a naming heuristic
findings.evidence: truncateAll() issues TRUNCATE ... RESTART IDENTITY CASCADE across six tables. The guard is a database-name substring check (db.includes('test')) plus a MURMUR_TEST_DB_CONFIRM opt-out. The repo's DATABASE_URL resolves to database name 'postgres' on the live Supabase host, so the heuristic does hold today and npm test would abort. The defect is that the control is a name convention: any future disposable DB not named *test* trains the operator to set MURMUR_TEST_DB_CONFIRM=i-am-disposable, after which the guard is permanently gone. ci.yml runs npm test (destructive suites included) unconditionally.
findings.provenance: manual:destructive-test-guard - code read tests/helpers/test-db.ts:28-56 + DATABASE_URL database-name parse
findings.fix_hint: Key the guard on an explicit allowlist of DSN hosts (localhost, the CI service host) rather than a substring of the database name, and refuse any host matching *.supabase.co outright.

findings.category: A03:2021 - dynamic code execution (not in the shipped entry graph)
findings.evidence: Two new Function(...) sites in the vendored Claude Design preview runtime, both already carrying upstream nosemgrep annotations. Not reachable from client/index.html -> /src/main.ts. Recorded for completeness and cross-referenced from SEC-013. The CDN loads it performs do use SRI hashes (support.js:1074-1078) - those three Base64HighEntropyString detect-secrets hits are the SRI digests and are false positives.
findings.fix_hint: No action required beyond SEC-013's CSP and keeping preview harnesses out of the served root.
